successors.name: Danelaw
successors.text: Yorkshire, the East Midlands and East Anglia: the 221 cells of the 877 shape

successors.name: Kievan Rus'
successors.text: Ladoga, Rostov, Novgorod and Beloozero: 89 cells

successors.name: Old Kingdom of Norway
successors.text: land that passed to the Old Kingdom of Norway's shape in 875 and 1035

successors.name: Kingdom of the Isles
successors.text: the 27 Hebridean and Manx cells of the 1028 shape

successors.name: Angevin Empire
successors.text: Dublin, Waterford, Wexford, Cork and Limerick

ledger.x: 793: the Viking Age begins.
800: Norse enclave on Shetland.
800: Norse enclave on the Faroes.
800: Norse enclave near Rostov.
814: a four-cell enclave on the Rügen coast appears.
825: Norse enclaves on Orkney and the Outer Hebrides.
825: a five-cell enclave at the Peene mouth appears.
840: Norse enclave on Caithness and Sutherland.
840: Cliopatria draws the Isle of Man as Norse.
840: a six-cell enclave at the Oder mouth (Wolin) appears.
847: the Norse conquer the Inner Hebrides; Skye and Argyll are Cliopatria's cells beside them, on the land of Dal Riata.

c. 850: the Danes rule Frisia. Viking expansion (paraphrase): c. 850 Lothair I acknowledged Rorik as ruler of most of Friesland. The year is the page's 'c.'; Lothair I's realm is Cliopatria's Middle Franks (850-899).
840s: Vikings settle at the mouth of the Garonne.
850: a base at Bayonne.
850: Cliopatria draws Limerick as Norse.
850: a seven-cell enclave at Truso on the Vistula lagoon appears.
853: the Norse kingdom of Dublin.
860: Cliopatria draws Waterford as Norse.
860: the Garonne bases drop out of Cliopatria's shape.
862: Rurik is invited to Novgorod.
866: Beloozero.
866: a 35-cell Danish cluster in Lincolnshire (the Mercian side).
867: the Danes take York.
869: East Anglia falls.
c. 870: Iceland is first settled. 'Iceland was first settled around 870' (Viking expansion); Ingólfr Arnarson 'settled with his family around 874' at Reykjavík; Settlement of Iceland: 'around 874'.
874: Mercia falls to the army.
875: settlement spreads over the west, south and north of Iceland.
875: Harald Fairhair takes the Northern Isles.
875: Cliopatria hands Caithness and Sutherland to the Old Kingdom of Norway with the Northern Isles.
875: a Danish foothold on the Dorset coast.
877: a Danish foothold at Exeter.
878: the Dorset foothold ends with Guthrum's defeat.
878: the Exeter foothold ends with Guthrum's defeat at Edington (878).
878: Guthrum's army holds the Chippenham country.
878: the Danelaw takes the settled land.
880: the Chippenham cells leave Cliopatria's shape.
882: Oleg unites the Varangian north under Kiev.
885: Viking rule of Frisia ends.
886: a Viking army on the Seine at Paris.
892: the Seine cluster leaves Cliopatria's shape.
892: a Danish army lands in Kent.
896: the Danish army gives up.
902: the Irish drive the Norse out of Dublin. Ívarr II was 'Driven from Dublin in 902 by native Irish'; 'Dublin abandoned by the Norse from 902 to 917'.
907: the Norse occupy Brittany.
907: the Norse occupy Brittany, the Loire estuary included.
917: the Norse return to Dublin.

c. 914-922: Cork is founded. Viking expansion (paraphrase): the Vikings returned in 914, 'led by the Uí Ímair', and in 'the next eight years' founded Waterford, Wexford, Cork and Limerick, Ireland's first large towns (the span 914-922 is derived from that phrase).
930: the age of settlement ends and the Althing meets.
936: Alan II lands at Dol.
937: the occupation ends everywhere but the Loire.
939: the last Norse leave the Loire.
939: Trans-la-Forêt.
947: the Baltic enclaves west of the Oder leave Cliopatria's shape for the Kingdom of Germany row.
947: a small enclave on the Pomeranian coast.
980: the Wolin cells leave Cliopatria's shape for Poland.
980: the Limerick cluster leaves Cliopatria's shape.
1000: the last Baltic cells leave Cliopatria's shape.
1021: the Norse at L'Anse aux Meadows.
1022: the camp is given up.
1035: the Faroes pass to the Old Kingdom of Norway.
1079: Godred Crovan takes Mann and founds the Crovan dynasty.
1085: the Hebrides pass to Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Isles.
1171: the Normans take Dublin.
1171: the last Norse enclave falls and the row ends.

wars.name: Great Heathen Army
wars.outcome: The Danes land in East Anglia in 865, take York (867), defeat East Anglia (869) and Mercia (874); Alfred defeats Guthrum at Edington in 878 and the Treaty of Alfred and Guthrum (886-890) fixes the Danelaw's boundary.

wars.name: Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte
wars.outcome: Rollo enters vassalage to Charles the Simple and becomes the first Norman count of Rouen; the Duchy of Normandy dossier carries the land from 911 (Cliopatria's 911-921 Viking shape is corrected to leave it out).

wars.name: Expulsion of the Norse from Dublin
wars.outcome: Ívarr II is driven from Dublin by the native Irish in 902; the Norse hold nothing there until Sigtryggr returns in 917 (914 in the Viking expansion article).

wars.name: Battle of Clontarf
wars.outcome: Máel Sechnaill Mór defeats the Dublin Vikings at Tara (980); Gaelic conquest of Dublin led by Máel Sechnaill in 988 (Kingdom of Dublin); Glenmama (999); Clontarf (1014) ended the Dublin Vikings' ability to threaten Ireland's most powerful kings.

wars.name: Reconquest of Brittany by Alan II
wars.outcome: Alan II lands at Dol in 936 with Æthelstan's aid, is master of most of Brittany by 937 with the Norsemen forced back to the Loire, and ends the occupation of 907 to about 939 at Trans-la-Forêt on 1 August 939.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Dublin
wars.outcome: The last king of Dublin is killed by the Norman conquerors in 1171 (the infobox says the Norman conquest was 1170).

certainty.note: Raiding bases and first settlements with no fixed frontier: every enclave is Cliopatria's approximate cluster of cells.
Scattered enclaves with no surveyed frontier.
